item.title: U.S. economy slowed in second quarter as Iran war weighs on growth
item.description: Dconomic activity weakened between April and June as energy costs surged, new government data shows.

item.title: Iran war appears to expand to Egypt's coast as drones hit gas port
item.description: Drone strikes hit gas vessels at an Egyptian port on the Mediterranean, as a poll shows little American support for the five-month war with Iran.

item.title: Canelo Álvarez says there's "not much left" for him to do in boxing
item.description: Professional boxer Saúl "Canelo" Álvarez spoke to "CBS Mornings" co-host Nate Burleson about when he'll know to walk away from the sport.

item.title: Possible Russian missile crashes in Poland during Russian attacks on Ukraine
item.description: Russian attacks across Ukraine killed at least eight people and an apparent Russian missile crashed in Poland, officials said.

item.title: Russia slams Ukraine with deadly strikes as Poland alleges Moscow breached NATO airspace
item.description: Russia struck Ukraine with deadly attacks overnight. Meanwhile, Polish leadership is blaming Russia for allegedly violating NATO airspace rules after a missile landed over its shared border with Ukraine. CBS News' Aidan Stretch reports.

item.title: Nearly two-thirds of kids have caffeine in their diet. Here's how it's impacting their health
item.description: A new report from the CDC found nearly two-thirds of American kids between the ages of 2 and 19 have caffeine in their diet. On average, it found kids had 19.4 milligrams of caffeine on a given day. CBS News medical correspondent Dr. Celine Gounder explains the impact on their health.

item.title: Todd Blanche's nomination for attorney general stalled by 2 Republican holdouts
item.description: The Senate vote to advance Todd Blanche's nomination for attorney general was postponed after two key Republicans threatened to vote against him. CBS News' Olivia Rinaldi explains.

item.title: Latest news on Iran war as U.S. launches barrage of strikes following surprise attack
item.description: Following a thwarted "surprise attack" from Iran, the U.S. leveled a new barrage of strikes against Iran. Retired Marine Col. Mark Cancian joins CBS News with more.

item.title: See the devastating destruction of the wildfires in this French town
item.description: Entire neighborhoods have been reduced to ash amid the devastating wildfires in France. While thousands of people are being allowed to return to their homes, nearly 80,000 people across southern France are still displaced. Ramy Inocencio reports.

item.title: Blanche's nomination for AG on hold over fate of DOJ's "anti-weaponization fund"
item.description: Republican Sen. John Cornyn has demanded formal modifications to an agreement the Justice Department made with President Trump to settle his lawsuit against the IRS.

item.title: Fed leaves interest rate unchanged, but could a hike come later this year?
item.description: The Federal Reserve on Wednesday chose to hold interest rates steady, though three officials voted for a hike. Kelly O'Grady explains what this means for consumers and if a rate hike could come later this year.

item.title: Dr. Fauci invokes the Fifth Amendment at Senate hearing on COVID pandemic
item.description: Dr. Fauci, the leader of the government response to the COVID-19 pandemic, refused to answer questions at a hearing on Wednesday, invoking his Fifth Amendment right more than 100 times. Some Senate Republicans are now threatening to hold Fauci in contempt of Congress. Caitlin Huey-Burns reports.

item.title: Japan earthquake death toll climbs as hopes wane for additional rescues
item.description: The Kumamoto prefectural government said the powerful earthquake that hit southwestern Japan earlier this week has now killed at least 25 people, although the true death toll was likely higher.

item.title: Why vote for Todd Blanche as attorney general is on hold
item.description: Two Republicans are threatening to vote against President Trump's pick for attorney general, Todd Blanche, which could sink his nomination. A Senate committee has postponed Thursday's vote. Weijia Jiang explains.

item.title: Historic flooding slams Northeast, causing major damage
item.description: Nearly a foot of rain fell in less than a day in parts of the Northeast during a historic flooding event. Rob Marciano has a look at the damage.

item.title: Battle against monster wildfire in France boosted by improving weather
item.description: George and Amal Clooney are among thousands of residents in southwest France still displaced by a massive wildfire, but crews are gaining control.

item.title: Montana man, impaled by trekking pole, hikes out of mountains to get help
item.description: A hiker climbing Montana's highest peak slipped and impaled himself on his trekking pole as he fell, then hiked six miles off the mountain along with two friends to get help, he says.

item.title: Reality Check: You CAN Afford to Start a Family | Money Moves with Jill Schlesinger
item.description: Most Gen Z and millennials say the cost of raising a child feels financially out of reach and many don't believe they can start a family within the next five years. Jill offers a reality check: if you want kids, don't let fear stop you. Joined by special guest host Kayla Sabbagh of Greenspring Advisors, Jill and Mark explain why raising kids in this economy is more achievable than you think. Plus: 23-year-old Brianna, who still lives with her parents, calls in for guidance.

item.title: White House levels new allegation that China swept up voter data
item.description: The Trump administration on Thursday reiterated its view that China's alleged efforts to collect millions of American voter registration files constituted election interference.

item.title: Why is FIFA Forward Enterprise met with negativity from soccer organizations around the world?
item.description: A little more than a month after a very successful World Cup, FIFA, the world governing body of soccer, is cooking up something new. It's given member organizations and clubs until Sept. 19 to sign off on a proposed plan to sell shares of its most prestigious tournaments, and it's causing some controversy. Margaret Fleming, who reports on the business of soccer for Front Office Sports, has more.

item.title: DOJ asking secretive court to remove Afghan woman allegedly tied to terror plot
item.description: The DOJ is seeking to deport an Afghan woman who prosecutors allege is an "alien terrorist," in the first-ever test case before a secretive court that has never convened since it was created three decades ago.

item.title: Husband of U.S. woman missing in Grenada doesn't suspect foul play
item.description: The husband of a North Carolina woman who went missing last week​ while visiting the Caribbean island of Grenada said Wednesday he believes "there was no foul play" in her disappearance.

item.title: Salman Rushdie attacker convicted in terrorism trial over 2022 stabbing
item.description: A man has been convicted of federal terrorism charges in the 2022 stabbing that severely injured author Salman Rushdie.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy murder trial centers on ex's 911 call: "She killed the kids"
item.description: Prosecutors allege Lindsay Clancy made a "calculated decision" in killing her kids, while the defense says she was overmedicated and suffering from extreme postpartum psychosis.

item.title: Dr. Deborah Birx: Fauci hearing shows there's still anger over handling of COVID
item.description: Dr. Deborah Birx offered "The Takeout" her takeaways on what the contentious Senate hearing with former colleague Dr. Anthony Fauci says about the nation's ability to move on from COVID.

item.title: New DOJ rule would allow immigration judges to hold lawyers in contempt
item.description: The Justice Department is proposing a new rule to empower federal immigration judges to hold attorneys, their clients and witnesses in contempt if they violate court orders.

item.title: Fed holds interest rates steady, but 3 officials vote for hike
item.description: Fed officials are leaving their benchmark rate unchanged for a fifth straight meeting, a sign they expect inflation to ease.

item.title: FTC sues Hims & Hers, alleging it shared health data with Meta, Snap
item.description: Telehealth platform disclosed users' "most private" health info and locked consumers into subscriptions, regulators allege.

item.title: Singer-songwriter Glen Hansard killed in motorcycle crash
item.description: Academy Award-winning Irish singer-songwriter Glen Hansard has died in a motorcycle crash.

item.title: Actor Jared Leto accused of criminal sexual conduct by 4 women
item.description: Four women say Hollywood star Jared Leto committed sexual crimes against them when they were teenagers, in interviews with the BBC.
